problem:
Compute $P(X>-1)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{28}({x}^{2}+1),\, & -2\le x\le 2, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a<X\le b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is identical to zero for all $x>2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>-1) & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}\frac{3}{28}({x}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{28}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{x}^{2}+1\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{28}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+x]}_{-1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{28}([\frac{1}{3}(2)^{3}+(2)]-[\frac{1}{3}(-1)^{3}+(-1)]) \\  & =\frac{3}{28}([\frac{8}{3}+2]-[-\frac{1}{3}-1]) \\  & =\frac{3}{28}\cdot 6 \\  & =\frac{9}{14}.\end{aligned}
$$
